answer: Admission is priced like a cliff path, not a door. A newcomer stakes a bond on the ledge that unlocks only after a season of correct work, so a rented identity pays rent for the time a real one serves. Credit accrues on a terrace: one narrow step per epoch, its height set by work others already verified, each step reachable only from the one beneath, so an account bought late begins at the bottom stair. Each identity also carries a sable mark, a brush signature that smears when one credential runs on two machines at once, exposing the sharing. Copies inherit step count, never verified work.
